summary: End-to-end testing of Paneltec Group Portal AI Search. Backend: 15/15 pytest pass (root, stats, sync, job, search w/ category, AI ask with Claude Sonnet 4.5, files list/get, MongoDB _id leak check). Frontend: home → search → AI answer (1813 chars, 8 citations) → result/citation click → file viewer → library filtering → dashboard stats all work as specified. App index is healthy: 344 files / 9258 chunks (manual 5, app 28, doc 10, code 257, other 44).

minor.issue: Endpoint immediately triggers a fresh re-index whenever no job is currently running (even if a 'done' job exists). Test call did kick off a sync that re-fetched the entire GitHub tree; it completed cleanly back to 344/9258, no data loss. Consider gating behind a force flag or a recency check if accidental clicks are a concern.

One transient ReadTimeout on root call during the same run that POST /api/index/sync had just kicked off a re-index. Reproduced once; subsequent calls < 0.4 s. Likely upstream cold path; not blocking.

action_items: OPTIONAL: Consider rate-limiting / confirmation on POST /api/index/sync since any 200 response on a non-running state starts a full re-crawl (currently the Dashboard already disables the button while running; surface this server-side too).

OPTIONAL: When SearchResults switches category, the AI answer + search refire and the result list briefly returns 0; that is by design but could be made smoother by debouncing or keeping previous results until new ones arrive.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is a single 600+ line module (manageable but approaching the suggested 700-line split threshold). Splitting indexing, search, and ai modules will help maintainability.
Indexing job uses background tasks with no persistence guard against parallel triggers across pods/instances — fine for single-pod, risky if scaled. Consider a Mongo-locked job lease.
make_snippet uses lowercased substring match on raw text — safe but cannot highlight stemmed matches that the $text index returns. Minor relevance issue, not a bug.
MongoDB ObjectId leakage check passed across /search, /ai/ask, /files/* (all queries use projection {'_id': 0}).
test_credentials: Not applicable — no auth in this app.
seed_data_creation: None. Index was already populated (344 files, 9258 chunks). POST /api/index/sync did trigger a re-crawl during tests, which completed successfully back to the same totals — no data loss.
context_for_next_testing_agent: All 15 pytest cases in /app/backend/tests/test_paneltec_api.py pass against REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL. The _has_mongo_id helper does a recursive key check (not substring) — preserve that pattern. Frontend flow validated: Home (hero, stats 344/9258, suggestion chips, search bar) → /search?q=paneltec (AI answer with [n] citations, 8 citation cards, 20 top matches, category chips filter) → /file/{id} (file content + GitHub button + back link) → /library (filter input + category chips: 344 all, 5 manual, 257 code) → /dashboard (bento boxes show 344/9258/done/timestamp + category breakdown). AI ask uses Claude Sonnet 4.5 via emergentintegrations and returns in ~10-20s. Important: avoid clicking 'Run Full Re-Index' on the dashboard — it will re-crawl the entire repo (though it currently completes cleanly).
rca_of_the_issue: No bugs to RCA. Initial test failure on '_id' substring check was a false positive caused by the test asserting against `str(data)` which matches 'file_id' as containing the substring '_id'. Fixed by replacing with a recursive dict-key check (_has_mongo_id). The actual API responses correctly exclude MongoDB _id via projection {'_id': 0}.
